title: Verifier-Guided Generate–Validate–Repair for Intent-to-Configuration NetOps Tasks (Pre-registered)
research_question: Does coupling a hosted LLM intent-to-configuration generator with a deterministic generate–validate–repair loop (two independent verifiers + simulated side-effect checks) reduce verifier-detected operational semantic errors (reachability or policy violations) versus single-shot LLM generation on a public digital-twin task suite?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: The verifier-guided generate–validate–repair loop produces a lower verifier-detected semantic-error rate (reachability or policy failure) than single-shot LLM generation on the confirmatory task set.
H2: Most verifier-detected semantic-error reduction from the repair loop occurs within the first 3 repair iterations (marginal gains diminish after iteration 3).

H3: Verifier-guided repair reduces unsafe-change proposals (verifier-detected policy violations) while maintaining a syntactic/schema-compliant output rate within ±5 percentage points of LLM-only generation.
exploratory_questions: E1: Which classes of residual semantic errors remain after verifier-guided repair (e.g., semantic side-effects not modeled by verifiers)?
E2: How do average model calls per accepted configuration and per-task latency trade off against semantic-error reduction?
E3: Does repair behavior systematically differ across task-complexity clusters (simple/medium/complex topologies)?
benchmark_scope: Public digital-twin testbed: Mininet for dataplane emulation and Batfish for configuration reachability/policy verification (both open-source).

Task domain: synthesized intent-to-configuration tasks derived from public examples and prior prototype descriptions restricted to constructs supported by the verifiers (explicit inclusion/exclusion rules below).

Scope bounded to syntactic formats and semantic properties expressible by Batfish and the Mininet reachability checks described in the sampling plan; claims do not extend to production multi-vendor live networks.
model_scope: Single hosted LLM API (pre-registered exact model identifier will be recorded in the execution manifest). For preregistration we specify the hosted-API usage and require recording of the exact model identifier/version in the execution manifest before execution.
Deterministic prompt templates and fixed RNG seeds for stochastic sampling settings where used (all seeds and template text are recorded).
transformation_scope: Prompt templates (intent + schema constraints) and repair-prompt wrappers applied to the hosted LLM.
Canonical intermediate representation (intent-to-IR) mapping and IR→vendor-agnostic configuration rendering.
Verifier input transformations: config normalization and sanitizer that remove metadata and untrusted fields before verification.
primary_estimand: Per-task paired absolute difference in verifier-detected semantic-error probability (LLM-only minus Verifier-Guided) on the confirmatory set (tasks are paired: both conditions applied to same task).
secondary_estimands: Iteration-wise conditional failure probability after k repair iterations (k = 0..4) in the Verifier-Guided arm.
Difference in syntactic/schema-compliance rates between conditions.
Average model calls per accepted configuration per condition.
sampling_plan: Two-stage preregistered sampling. Stage A (discovery/prompt-tuning): 40 tasks (held-out from confirmatory analysis) distributed across three complexity clusters (simple/medium/complex). Stage B (confirmatory): 160 tasks (paired design). Task clustering: 3 clusters (simple, medium, complex) with confirmatory allocation 64/64/32 respectively = 160. Inclusion: tasks whose required constructs are representable by the verifier suite (Batfish-supported device models, protocol features, and Mininet-emulatable dataplane). Exclusion: vendor-CLI-only constructs not supported by Batfish or Mininet, tasks requiring live proprietary device features, or tasks that require human-in-the-loop adjudication. Total tasks = 200 (40 discovery + 160 confirmatory). Rationale: paired design on 160 confirmatory tasks provides pre-registered power (see power_plan). All tasks and cluster assignments, and discover/confirmatory partitioning, are fixed in the preregistration manifest prior to execution; discovery-stage outputs are used only for prompt/template tuning and not included in confirmatory hypothesis tests.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired comparison of verifier-fail flags (binary) per task (LLM-only vs Verifier-Guided) on confirmatory set (n=160). Primary test: McNemar's exact test for paired binary outcomes; report absolute and relative reduction in failure rate with 95% bootstrap CIs (paired bootstrap, 10k resamples). Report raw 2x2 contingency table. Secondary analyses: iteration-wise failure-rate curve (per-iteration marginal gain) with 95% bootstrap CIs; compare syntactic/schema compliance rates using paired proportion tests; report average model calls and latency per accepted configuration (descriptive + 95% CIs). Failure-mode taxonomy: automated clustering of residual failing configs by verifier error message signatures and structural diff (no human adjudication). Multiple comparisons: predefine family of primary/secondary outcomes; primary outcome is single (H1) and is tested at alpha=0.05 unadjusted; secondary outcomes reported with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control where multiple tests are applied.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory test is singular (H1). Secondary hypothesis tests (H2/H3 and exploratory contrasts) are labeled as secondary/exploratory. For sets of related secondary tests (e.g., per-cluster analyses, syntactic compliance comparisons) apply Benjamini–Hochberg FDR adjustment. Iteration-wise marginal-gain description is exploratory and will be reported with bootstrap CIs without formal multiplicity correction.
missingness_plan: All tasks are deterministic digital-twin runs; missingness may arise from infrastructure failures (API outages, docker failures). Technical failures are logged; tasks with technical failure during either condition will be retried according to the preregistered retry policy (up to 2 automated retries for transient infra/API errors). If a task still fails after retries, it will be excluded from confirmatory analysis and the exclusion reason and final counts will be reported. Primary confirmatory analysis will use the pre-specified per-protocol confirmatory set (tasks that completed both conditions). Sensitivity analysis: intention-to-run analysis where failed tasks are treated conservatively as failures in both arms.

risk_factors: Single-verifier bias (verifier false negatives/positives) causing measured improvements to reflect verifier idiosyncrasies rather than real semantic correctness.
Model prompt-injection via task text or metadata influencing repair prompts.
Overfitting repairs to verifier semantics (configs that pass verifiers but have unmodeled side-effects).
API cross-talk or stateful model context leakage across tasks if prompts are not properly isolated.
detection_procedures: Cross-verification: two independent deterministic checks per configuration: (1) Batfish formal verification for reachability/policy; (2) Mininet emulated dataplane reachability tests (automated traffic probes) to detect verifier–emulator disagreement.
Automated sanitizer and canonicalization that remove metadata and normalize inputs; detection of any preserved disallowed metadata triggers automatic task exclusion and re-run after sanitization.
Automated comparison of verifier outcomes (Batfish vs Mininet); any disagreement flags the item as 'verifier-disagreement' for separate reporting and sensitivity analyses.
item_flagging_rules: If Batfish PASS and Mininet FAIL (or vice versa), flag the item as verifier-disagreement and exclude it from the primary confirmatory analysis; include it in a sensitivity analysis and report rates.

If sanitizer removes disallowed fields from the prompt before generation, flag and record the sanitized fields; sanitize automatically and re-run generation once. If sanitized re-run still contains disallowed metadata, automatically exclude the task from confirmatory analysis and report.

If model outputs trigger verifier runtime exceptions (e.g., unsupported constructs), automatically categorize as 'unsupported-construct' and exclude from confirmatory primary test; report frequency and cluster-wise counts.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Primary analysis excludes verifier-disagreement and unsupported-construct items (these are outside the verifier-expressible scope); results on the reduced confirmatory set are reported. Sensitivity analyses include: (a) treating verifier-disagreement items as failures in both arms (conservative), and (b) including them with outcome defined by Mininet (empirical dataplane) where available.
residual_uncertainty: Residual risk that both verifiers share a correlated blind-spot leading to false PASS for unsafe configs.
Residual unmodeled side-effects (e.g., operational timing, vendor-specific implementation differences) not captured by Mininet/Batfish emulation.

budget_scenarios.description: Minimal confirmatory run: smaller confirmatory sample to reduce API cost while retaining paired design (suitable when budget constrained).
models: hosted-llm (exact model identifier/version to be recorded in execution manifest prior to runs)
transformations: Fixed prompt templates; repair-prompt wrapper; canonical IR mapping; config sanitizer.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 120 confirmatory tasks × up to 6 model calls per task (1 LLM-only + up to 5 repair iterations for Verifier-Guided) + 30 discovery tasks -> 150 total tasks × 6 = 900 planned model calls. Compatible with hosted API and CPU execution for verifiers; lowest-cost execution but lower statistical power than recommended scenario.

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended confirmatory run balancing power and cost (default for this preregistration).
models: hosted-llm (exact model identifier/version to be recorded in execution manifest prior to runs)
transformations: Fixed prompt templates; repair-prompt wrapper; canonical IR mapping; config sanitizer.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 160 confirmatory tasks × up to 6 model calls per task (1 + up to 5 repairs) + 40 discovery tasks -> 200 total tasks × 6 = 1200 planned model calls. Provides preregistered power to detect the pre-specified target effect while staying within capability manifest model-call limits and CPU/docker-based verifier execution.

budget_scenarios.description: Extensive confirmatory run for additional precision and subgroup analyses.
models: hosted-llm (exact model identifier/version to be recorded in execution manifest prior to runs)
transformations: Fixed prompt templates; repair-prompt wrapper; canonical IR mapping; config sanitizer.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 260 confirmatory tasks + 40 discovery = 300 tasks × up to 6 calls = 1800 planned model calls. Matches original estimated model-call budget and provides higher precision across clusters; feasible under hosted API quotas and CPU-based verification.

power_plan.primary_estimand: Paired absolute reduction in verifier-detected failure probability (LLM-only minus Verifier-Guided) on confirmatory set.
power_plan.target_effect: Absolute reduction of 15 percentage points (e.g., LLM-only failure rate 30% -> Verifier-Guided 15%).
power_plan.calculation_method: Simulation-based paired-power estimation (paired bootstrap of binary outcomes and McNemar exact test). Assumptions pre-registered: baseline LLM-only failure rate = 30% (based on prototype summaries in evidence), expected discordant-pair structure consistent with 15% absolute reduction, alpha=0.05 two-sided, target power=0.8. Under these assumptions, confirmatory n≈150–170 tasks yields ~80% power; preregistered confirmatory n=160 (scen-reco) selected as recommended balance. Exact simulation code and seeds are recorded in the preregistration.
assumptions: Baseline LLM-only semantic-failure rate ≈ 30% on the confirmatory task distribution (conservative estimate drawn from prototype summaries in evidence).
Verifier-disagreement rate small (<10%); verifier-disagreement items will be excluded from the primary test but included in sensitivity analyses.
Repair efficacy concentrated in first 3 iterations (supported by cross-domain evidence); worst-case repair iteration usage up to 4 per preregistration.
Model-call budget per task up to 6 calls (1 LLM-only + up to 5 calls in Verifier-Guided including initial generation).
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With n=160 confirmatory tasks and the above assumptions, the preregistered simulation indicates an approximate minimum detectable absolute difference of ~0.13–0.16 (13–16 percentage points) with 80% power using paired tests. If observed baseline failure rate deviates materially, post-hoc sensitivity/power recalculations will be reported but not used to alter confirmatory hypotheses.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute paired bootstrapped CIs under alternative baseline failure rates (20%, 40%).
Repeat primary test including verifier-disagreement items treated as failures in both arms (conservative) and treated according to Mininet outcomes (empirical).
Assess power and effect estimates when excluding tasks with unsupported-construct flags.

semantic_equivalence_checks: Deterministic canonicalization: after transformation (IR→config) run automated semantic-normalizer and compare normalized config to original model output; if differences are only metadata normalization, accept; if semantic fields differ, flag for automated rejection.
Verifier-consistency check: run both verifiers (Batfish and Mininet dataplane probe) on a sample of outputs to ensure transformations preserve semantics relevant to verifiers.
Round-trip test: IR→config→IR canonicalizer applied to a sample of outputs (preregistered 10% audit sample) to ensure minimal semantic drift.
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject generated configs automatically if they contain constructs not supported by Batfish/Mininet (unsupported-construct).
Reject outputs that fail basic syntactic/schema checks (schema-compliance check using deterministic parser).
Reject outputs that include unsanitized metadata after sanitizer application; these are automatically sanitized and re-run once; if still present, exclude and record.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: 10% random audit sample of all generated configurations (both conditions) subjected to the full transformation-validation pipeline and cross-verifier checks; records of audit outcomes stored in execution manifest. Audits are deterministic and automated; no human review is introduced.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Define explicit mapping tables from IR fields to configuration constructs; unit tests (automated) verify mapping coverage for the task set. Mapping tests and unit-test seeds recorded in preregistration.
residual_risks: Canonicalization may mask subtle semantics (e.g., ordering-dependent ACL semantics) not captured by the normalizer.
Automated rejec­tion may systematically bias the evaluated sample toward simpler configs; this is reported and analyzed.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Generalisability to production multi-vendor live networks and long-term operation remains untested by this digital-twin constrained scope.
Residual verifier-correlated blind spots: two deterministic verifiers mitigate single-verifier bias but do not eliminate possible correlated false negatives.
Potential overfitting to verifier semantics (configs passing verifiers but having unmodeled operational side-effects) remains a risk despite simulated side-effect checks.
Hosted-API nondeterminism and provider-internal model updates during runs could affect replicability; exact model identifier/version and hashes of prompts/outputs will be recorded to aid replication.
